Replicating the thesis

Source: vignettes/thesis-replication.Rmd
thesis-replication.Rmd

The model of lexio was introduced in Rocha (2026), which applies it to two energy markets of Brazil with the 2018 input-output matrix with energy-sector detail published by EPE and FIPE (72 sectors). This vignette shows how that application is declared and run. The code is not run when the vignette is built, because the data are distributed apart from the package; the folder replication/ of the repository (https://github.com/FilipeVascRocha/lexio) runs everything, as described in its README.md.

The application

Market Entrant (>=) Incumbent (<=) Labour (>=) Shock
Electricity GD, distributed generation GC, centralized generation LAB, +1% 1% of b_GD + b_GC, to GD or to GC
Fuels CR, biodiesel + ethanol CNR, petroleum products + natural gas LAB, +5% 5% of b_CR + b_CNR, to CR or to CNR
  • The entrant energy is a floor and the incumbent a ceiling: the entrant should not fall below its goal and the incumbent should not exceed its goal.
  • Each scenario gives the shock to one of the two energy sources; the other keeps its base, and labour grows by the share of the shock.
  • The economic block is (I − A) x ≥ f, at the last level, with absolute deviations.
  • The corridor α_h is the intersectoral purchase of the energy products of the market divided by the output of sector h, on both sides.
  • The six orderings of the three accounts are run in each scenario, with the exact lock: 2 markets × 2 scenarios × 6 orderings = 24 runs of 4 levels.

The data

The database is the file lexio-thesis-data-2018.zip, attached to the GitHub release of lexio and archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24293808); replication/01_declare_data.R builds the same files from the public workbook of EPE. The file also holds a dictionary of every file and column (thesis_data/metadata.xlsx) and the EPE workbook itself, unchanged (data/), so that the database can be rebuilt even if the workbook leaves the EPE site. For each market:

thesis_data/fuels/
  base/            sectors, Z, x, f, E (levels of CR, CNR and LAB) and corridor, as published
  model.yml        the model, with the goals declared by their rules
  coefficients/    B = I - A, D, x, f and corridor, rounded to 15 significant digits
  model_exact.yml  the same model, with the goals rounded in the same way

The thesis stored the coefficients and the goals with 15 significant digits between its steps. coefficients/ and model_exact.yml keep that rounding, so the problem is identical to the one solved in the thesis; base/ and model.yml give the same numbers up to about 1e-9.

Declaring the fuels model in R

The coefficients, read into vectors:

library(lexio)
dir <- "replication/thesis_data/fuels/coefficients"
read_table <- function(name) {
  read.csv(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(code = "character"))
}
sectors <- read_table("sectors")
B <- as.matrix(read_table("B")[, -1])
x <- read_table("x")$value
f <- read_table("f")$value
D <- read_table("D")
alpha <- read_table("corridor")$alpha

io <- declare_io(B = B, x = x, f = f,
                 D = list(CR = D$CR, CNR = D$CNR, LAB = D$LAB),
                 corridor = alpha, sectors = sectors)
io

The model: the directions, the goals of the two scenarios and the six orderings.

shock <- list(type = "pooled_share", share = 0.05, pool = c("CR", "CNR"))
model <- define_model(
  accounts = list(
    CR  = list(direction = ">=", target = list(type = "base"), unit = "toe"),
    CNR = list(direction = "<=", target = list(type = "base"), unit = "toe"),
    LAB = list(direction = ">=", target = list(type = "growth", rate = 0.05), unit = "jobs")
  ),
  economy = list(direction = ">=", target = "final_demand", position = "last", deviation = "absolute"),
  scenarios = list(CR = list(CR = shock), CNR = list(CNR = shock)),
  priorities = "all",
  corridor = list(use = TRUE, multiplier = 1),
  lock_tolerance = "exact",
  name = "thesis_fuels"
)

The goal of each account is its total level in the scenario, not the shock alone. With the bases b_CR = 19,882,543 toe, b_CNR = 110,028,128 toe and b_LAB = 97,776,839 jobs, the shock is 0.05 × (b_CR + b_CNR) = 6,495,534 toe, and

Scenario Goal of CR Goal of CNR Goal of LAB
CR 26,378,077 (base + shock) 110,028,128 (base) 102,665,681 (base × 1.05)
CNR 19,882,543 (base) 116,523,662 (base + shock) 102,665,681

satellite_base(io) and build_goals(io, model, "CR") return these numbers.

Running and reading the results 

res <- run_model(io, model)
res
write_outputs(res, "outputs_fuels")

results.xlsx, in the output folder, holds every result. Its result sheets have one row per row of G: xD1, xD2 and xD3 (CR, CNR and LAB) and f'1 to f'72 (the sectors).

Result Sheet
the last level of the six orderings, side by side (g; Gx, d_minus, d_plus and x of each ordering) final_CR, final_CNR
every level (stage) of one ordering, side by side CR_P01 … CNR_P06
Gx − g Gx_CR, Gx_CNR
sectoral output x* and Δx x_CR, x_CNR
the optimum of each level and the change in each account runs
base, goal and achieved value of each account goals
the distinct final states states

The orderings P01 to P06 are, for the fuels market, CR-CNR-LAB, CR-LAB-CNR, CNR-CR-LAB, CNR-LAB-CR, LAB-CR-CNR and LAB-CNR-CR, each followed by the economic block.

The published numbers

replication/02_reproduce.R runs both markets with coefficients/ and model_exact.yml and compares 12 indicators with the values printed in the thesis:

Number Published
Largest share of the shock realized by GD 31.0%
Largest share of the shock realized by CR 27.2%
Co-movement at the frontier, GC per GD 6.06 toe/toe
Co-movement at the frontier, CNR per CR 4.42 toe/toe
Fuels frontier: change in output R$ 284.8 billion (2.39%)
Fuels frontier: change in jobs 1.72 million
State with CNR at its goal: change in output R$ 254.4 billion (2.13%)
State with CNR at its goal: change in jobs 1.63 million
Distinct states: electricity, fuels 5, 4

The script ends with 12 of 12 published numbers match and with every level of the 24 runs optimal. The model declared above, with the goals written as rules, gives the same 9 fuels numbers.

Reference

Rocha, F. V. (2026). Modelo generalizado de insumo-produto com Goal Programming preemptivo aplicado à transição energética brasileira: eletricidade e combustíveis na estrutura produtiva de 2018. Doctoral thesis, Programa de Pós-graduação em Economia, Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora.
